data.narrative:
NuScale Power operates in the nuclear energy sector as a public-stage company that has raised $600M+ to date. The comparable universe for nuclear energy remains sparse: three public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and six private competitors including Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy. This fragmented landscape reflects the capital intensity and regulatory complexity of the sector.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The nuclear energy subsector lacks a sufficiently dense peer set at matching stage and valuation tier; only one same-stage comparable was identified within nuclear, falling well short of the three-datapoint minimum required for robust median analysis. Expanding to all nuclear sector peers would obscure material differences in technology, capital structure, and commercialization timeline, introducing substantial noise rather than signal.

The sparsity of comparable data points represents the primary valuation constraint. Without triangulation to peer multiples, alternative methods—discounted cash flow, precedent transactions, or forward revenue multiples—would need to anchor any valuation range. The public comps (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and identified private peers offer directional reference but cannot support a narrow, defensible valuation band on their own. Further data collection on capital deployment rates, technology de-risking milestones, and regulatory approval timelines across the peer set would be required to establish conviction on value.
